systems.name: Skin & soft tissue
systems.operation: Patch the Cut on the Arm
targets: Skin is the body's outer shield and keeps germs out.
A scrape or cut is a break in that shield.
Clean before close - dirt left under a bandage is a bad idea.
Bandages and gentle stitches help edges meet so skin can heal.
Hands off real wounds - real care needs a grown-up / clinic.
scenarios: Scraped knee after playground fall - dirt + sting, not horror.
Small forearm cut from cardboard edge - clean line, blue gel mess.
Bandage put on dirty cut (wrong path) - Pip teaches redo.
steps: 1. notice: Spot cut on arm board (pass: Tap I see the cut)
2. predict: Choose clean first (pass: Correct hypothesis)
3. act: Remove blue mess (pass: clear>=90) tool=sponge
4. act: Antiseptic along guide (pass: cover guide zone) tool=swab
5. act: Connect dots 1 to 4 (pass: order + path OK) tool=needle
6. act: Protect while healing (pass: snap to ghost) tool=bandage
7. observe: Vitals green; closed icon (pass: stable)
8. journal: Why clean before stitch? (pass: fields>=2)
systems.fairTest: Does a dirty vs clean sponge leave more mess markers? Count remaining markers; journal which was better.
systems.journal: Name one skin job. Why did we sponge before the needle?

systems.name: Bones & joints
targets: Bones are the hard frame that holds shape and protects soft parts.
Joints are places bones meet so we can bend.
A fracture means a bone broke or cracked (cartoon gap).
Align -> hold still -> cast/splint helps bone heal straight.
Real broken bones need real doctors - this game teaches ideas only.
scenarios: Arm bone clean break gap after tree-climb slip story.
Twisted ankle joint - swollen soft pad, rest + wrap.
Cast put on before align (wrong) - Pip blocks.
steps: 1. notice: See gap on inset (pass: toggle on) tool=xray
2. predict: Align before cast (pass: correct gate)
3. act: Ends meet (pass: snap ghost) tool=align
4. act: Keeps still (pass: snap) tool=splint
5. act: Hard shell (pass: wrap>=95) tool=cast
6. observe: Gap closed glow (pass: green check) tool=xray
7. journal: Why align first? (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: Loose vs snug cast - which keeps bone ghost aligned after jiggle?
systems.journal: What does a cast do? What happens if we cast before aligning?

systems.name: Muscles & tendons
targets: Muscles pull on bones to make movement.
Tendons are tough strings connecting muscle to bone.
A strain is overstretched muscle - needs rest and gentle care.
In this game, comfort tools are diagram demonstrations; real pain needs adult help.
Never force a hurt muscle - stop and tell a grown-up in real life.
scenarios: Calf strain after too much running in PE.
Sore shoulder from backpack - tired muscle meter.
Stretching hard while strained (wrong) - rest first.
steps: 1. notice: Find strain glow (pass: tap correct muscle)
2. predict: Rest first (pass: correct order)
3. act: Cool comfort (pass: cover>=80) tool=ice
4. act: Quiet healing (pass: timer complete) tool=rest
5. act: After rest only (pass: stay in corridor) tool=stretch
6. act: Support (pass: snap) tool=wrap
7. journal: Rest before stretch? (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: Stretch immediately vs rest then stretch - which lowers glow faster?
systems.journal: What do muscles do? Why rest a strain before hard stretch?

systems.name: Blood & clotting lite
targets: Blood carries oxygen and helpers through pipe vessels.
When a small cut happens, clotting helpers form a soft plug.
Pressure + bandage help the plug team (idea only).
Lots of bleeding in real life = get a grown-up / emergency help.
No gore: blue/teal flow chips or soft coral dots, never spurts.
scenarios: Small finger nick - clotting demo.
Nosebleed calm sit-forward tip card.
Running around with open nick (wrong).
steps: 1. notice: See flow chips leaving cut (pass: tap)
2. act: Helpers stick (pass: hold meter) tool=pressure
3. act: Slow flow (pass: pose match) tool=elevate
4. observe: Watch clot form (pass: wait bar) tool=observeHelpers
5. act: Protect plug (pass: snap) tool=bandage
6. journal: What helps a clot? (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: With vs without pressure pad - time for clot meter to fill.
systems.journal: Name one job of blood. How do platelet helpers help a small cut?

systems.name: Heart & circulation
targets: Heart is a pump that pushes blood in a loop.
Arteries/veins are pipes (out/return colors).
Healthy habits help the pump.
A path block puzzle teaches flow - not real transplant surgery.
Real chest pain / fainting = real emergency - not a game level.
anatomy: Loop pipes to body and lungs
scenarios: Path pipe disconnected - reconnect snap.
Valve flap stuck closed - tap rhythm.
Lazy habit meter - choose healthy cards.
steps: 1. notice: Weak pulse wave (pass: tap heart)
2. act: Hear flow (pass: correct zone) tool=stethoscope
3. act: Restore loop (pass: snap) tool=coupler
4. act: Open gate (pass: rhythm taps) tool=valve
5. act: Everyday care (pass: pick 2 healthy) tool=habits
6. observe: Strong pulse (pass: green waveform)
7. journal: What does the heart do? (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: Count pulse waves on habit boost vs no boost (visual meter).
systems.journal: Is the heart a pump or a filter? Name one heart-healthy habit.

systems.name: Lungs & breathing
systems.theme: Air in/out; airway clear; calm inhaler/ER
targets: Lungs take oxygen in and send carbon dioxide out.
Airway is the path from nose/mouth to lungs - keep it clear.
Calm breathing helps when scared or wheezy.
Inhaler / helper puff is a tool some kids use - learn respect, not self-dose.
Real can't-breathe emergency = get adults / call for help.
scenarios: Soft clog in airway cartoon.
Fast scared breathing after fall - calm belly-breath.
Asthma-like wheeze vignette - adult + inhaler respect.
steps: 1. notice: Low O2 band (pass: tap vitals)
2. act: Open path (pass: pose match) tool=situp
3. act: Air needs open tube (pass: remove clog) tool=forceps
4. act: Calm cycles (pass: 3 cycles) tool=breaths
5. act: Respect ask adult (pass: correct card order) tool=inhaler
6. observe: O2 green (pass: stable)
7. journal: Path of air? (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: Belly breath vs shoulder shrug - which raises calm meter faster?
systems.journal: Trace air from nose to lungs. What should you do if someone really can't breathe?

systems.name: Digestion
targets: Food travels: mouth -> esophagus -> stomach -> intestines.
Digestion breaks food into usable bits (plumbing + factory).
Upset stomach - rest, water, adult help (ideas).
Don't invent surgery for tummy aches.
Real severe pain = real care, not Arcade.
scenarios: Follow a food token through a connected educational digestion model.
Too much junk snack meter.
Ignoring water when tummy upset.
steps: 1. notice: Trace path (pass: label quiz) tool=viewer
2. act: Find soft plug (pass: tap bend)
3. act: Help move (pass: guide strokes) tool=pad
4. act: Care habits (pass: apply water+rest) tool=water
5. observe: Bolus passes (pass: exit to intestine)
6. journal: Name 3 path stops (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: Water+rest vs ignore-water on comfort meter.
systems.journal: List the food path in order. Why is digestion like plumbing?

systems.name: Kidneys / urine lite
targets: Kidneys are filters that clean the blood.
Cleaned leftover liquid becomes urine stored in the bladder.
Drinking water helps filters work (habit, not medical dose).
Pain / can't pee / blood in urine in real life = tell an adult.
Keep it lite - no graphic content.
scenarios: Filter mesh clogged with waste chips.
Low water meter.
Ignoring thirst on hot day.
steps: 1. notice: Dirty mesh (pass: tap kidney)
2. act: Sort waste chips (pass: correct bins) tool=sorter
3. act: Flush idea (pass: apply) tool=water
4. observe: Clear mesh (pass: green)
5. journal: What do kidneys filter? (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: High water vs low water - waste chips cleared per minute.
systems.journal: Kidneys are like what household tool? Why drink water?

systems.name: Brain & nerves lite
targets: Brain is the control hub; nerves are signal wires.
Signals tell muscles to move and bring touch messages back.
A head bump with symptoms needs stopping play, adult attention and professional assessment.
A quieter setting can feel more comfortable; a game quiz cannot assess a head injury.
Return to sport after suspected concussion needs healthcare professional clearance.
scenarios: After ball bonk story - rest the hub (no gore).
Tangled signal wire puzzle.
Jumping back into game too soon (wrong).
steps: 1. notice: Dizzy sparkles (pass: tap)
2. act: Rest helps (pass: toggle quiet) tool=dimmer
3. act: Tell grown-up (pass: affirm) tool=adult
4. act: Healing quiet (pass: timer) tool=quiet
5. observe: Check wires (pass: gentle quiz) tool=retest
6. journal: What are nerves? (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: Quiet rest vs noisy arcade - which clears dizzy sparkles faster?
systems.journal: Brain : hub :: nerves : ____. What do you do after a real head bump?

systems.name: Immune / germs vs body
targets: Immune team guards the body against germs.
Wash hands, sleep, food care help defenses.
White-cell heroes tag and clear germs (cartoon).
Vaccines / doctors are real-world helpers - respect.
Capstone: combine skin barrier + immune team.
scenarios: Germ blobs on unwashed hands before snack.
Skin cut open to germs - ties S1.
Skipping sleep - defense meter drops.
steps: 1. notice: Spot germ blobs (pass: tap)
2. act: Remove germs (pass: scrub meter) tool=soap
3. act: Close door (pass: snap) tool=bandage
4. act: Deploy helpers (pass: drag to germs) tool=cells
5. act: Boost defense (pass: pick cards) tool=habits
6. journal: Name 2 defenses (pass: required)
systems.fairTest: Wash vs no-wash before snack - germ count on hand print plate.
systems.journal: List two ways your body fights germs. What is one habit that helps?
